implemented_requirements.evidence: claw.py – In `Claw.update` when state is SWING the angle is incremented/decremented between ±CLAW_MAX_ANGLE, creating a back‑and‑forth motion.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Player times a grab to collect objects
implemented_requirements.evidence: game.py – `handle_events` calls `self.claw.launch()` on mouse click or SPACE/ENTER when playing; `Claw.launch` switches state to EXTEND, starting the grab.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Each object has a value and takes time to reel in
implemented_requirements.evidence: objects.py – `GameObject` stores `self.value` and `self.weight`; `Claw.update` uses `obj.reel_speed_factor` (weight) to adjust retract speed, making heavier objects slower.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Level ends when time runs out or minimum gold value is met
implemented_requirements.evidence: game.py – In `update`, `self.time_left` counts down; if `self.level_score >= self.target` the level is cleared, and if `self.time_left <= 0` the game ends.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Display the position of the claw and objects, updating after each grab
implemented_requirements.evidence: game.py – `draw` calls each object's `draw` method and `claw.draw`; `Claw.update` moves the attached object's coordinates to the tip each frame.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Introduce ascending difficulty with more obstacles or tighter time limits
implemented_requirements.evidence: settings.py – `get_level_config` returns higher swing/extend speeds, lower time limits, and increased counts of rocks, TNT, etc. `GoldMinerGame.load_level` applies these per level.

judge.summary: The provided source implements a functional Gold Miner game: a swinging claw that can be launched to grab objects, each object carrying a value and weight that influences reel‑in time, level progression based on a gold target or timer, visual rendering of the claw and objects, and a difficulty curve that tightens time limits and adds obstacles. All core requirements are present and the code appears ready to run with pygame (and optional numpy for sound). No show‑stopper issues were found.
